werk/joni-mitchell-for-the-roses.text:
For the Roses was released in November 1972, between Blue and Court and Spark, the two greatest successes of Joni Mitchell. It is her fifth studio album. Her record company asked for a song for radio. Mitchell wrote You Turn Me On I'm a Radio, intended as a sarcastic answer. It became her first top 40 hit under her own name. Cold Blue Steel and Sweet Fire is a menacing, jazzy portrait of the heroin addiction of her then boyfriend James Taylor. Judgement of the Moon and Stars was inspired by Beethoven.

The critics were glowing. The New York Times praised the elegant language and the irony, and Rolling Stone mentioned her vocal acting and phrasing. Robert Christgau heard how she had turned the strange leaps of her voice into music that sounded almost classical. In 2007 the Library of Congress added the album to the National Recording Registry.
werk/joni-mitchell-for-the-roses.listen: In Cold Blue Steel and Sweet Fire, listen to the mood of the song: notice how the jazzy, menacing sound suits the subject of the lyrics.

werk/joni-mitchell-hejira.text:
Joni Mitchell wrote the songs for this album while travelling in late 1975 and early 1976, among other things as a member of the Rolling Thunder Revue and during a drive across America. Jazz musicians can be heard on the record: Larry Carlton, John Guerin and above all Jaco Pastorius. After the basic tracks she met Pastorius, with whom she connected at once. She found the bass sounds of the sixties and early seventies dead and distant, and had him overdub his bass parts on four songs.

The album sounds like the journey itself: dense, sprawling songs, carried by her guitar and the fretless bass. The title is an Arabic word for departure, which she understood as running away with honour. Coyote, Amelia and Hejira became regulars in her concerts. The record sold less than its predecessors, but was well received and has since been regarded as a high point of her career.
werk/joni-mitchell-hejira.listen: Listen to Hejira and notice how Pastorius's fretless bass moves freely instead of merely playing the root of each chord.

werk/joni-mitchell-ladies-of-the-canyon.text:
Ladies of the Canyon is Joni Mitchell's third studio album and was released in 1970 on Reprise Records. The title refers to Laurel Canyon, the neighbourhood in Los Angeles where the pop music of the sixties flourished and where she lived herself, in the house that Graham Nash would later sing about in Our House. The album includes Big Yellow Taxi, Woodstock and The Circle Game.

The album shows a broader artistic outlook than her earlier work, with songs about fame, the Woodstock generation and the complexity of love. It is often seen as a transition between the folk-like beginnings and the more refined records that followed. Dense, wordless harmonies recall David Crosby, and in The Circle Game Crosby, Stills, Nash and Young sing along. Robert Christgau thought it better than her earlier work. Big Yellow Taxi became a standard and is often used to draw attention to environmental injustice.
werk/joni-mitchell-ladies-of-the-canyon.listen: Listen to Big Yellow Taxi and notice the lyrics, which are about DDT, among other things.

werk/joni-mitchell-the-hissing-of-summer.text:
On this record from November 1975, Joni Mitchell pushes the smooth jazz-pop of Court and Spark in a more adventurous direction. Members of L.A. Express and the Crusaders play on it, with contributions from James Taylor, David Crosby and Graham Nash. For the first time she uses synthesizers and experiments with sampling. The lyrics deal with women's experiences of patriarchal norms, with suburban life and with the music industry.

The Jungle Line features a loop of the Drummers of Burundi, the first commercially released track with a sample. Without a big hit, the record still reached number four in the United States. Critics initially reacted dismissively and found the work weaker than its predecessor, but it grew into one of her most acclaimed albums.
werk/joni-mitchell-the-hissing-of-summer.listen: Listen to The Jungle Line and notice the rhythmic loop of the Drummers of Burundi, beneath which guitar, synthesizer and vocals are layered.

werk/joost-klein-europapa.text: In March 2024 Europapa by Joost Klein, from Friesland, became a hit on TikTok and Spotify, reaching number one in the Netherlands and Flanders. The cheerful, chaotic song is about travelling freely through Europe, and also about his late father. After an incident behind the scenes, Joost was disqualified from the contest on 11 May, the day of the final in Malmö. The song remained popular afterwards.
werk/joost-klein-europapa.listen: Europapa sounds like a gabber party with a childlike chorus. Joost sings in Dutch and raps about the countries of Europe.

werk/joshua-redman-beyond.text:
Beyond is a 2000 studio album by saxophonist Joshua Redman, released by Warner Bros. It contains ten original compositions. Critics see its success in the musicians he invited: pianist Aaron Goldberg, bassist Reuben Rogers and drummer Gregory Hutchinson. Redman wanted to make the album a statement about their shared identity and wrote all the pieces with them in mind.

Mark Turner plays tenor saxophone on the fourth track. JazzTimes wrote that the compositions suggest Redman is going to live up to the hype. The Washington Post found the pieces logical and coherent, because he is working with familiar partners. The Buffalo News called it perhaps his best record to date. Courage (Asymmetric Aria) and Balance were used on the programme Local Forecast on The Weather Channel.
werk/joshua-redman-beyond.listen: Listen to Leap of Faith and notice the guest soloist Mark Turner on tenor saxophone.

werk/joshua-redman-freedom-in-the-groove.text:
Freedom in the Groove was released in 1996 as a studio album by the American jazz saxophonist Joshua Redman. He wrote and arranged all the pieces himself. He plays tenor, soprano and alto saxophone, with Peter Bernstein on electric guitar, Peter Martin on piano, Chris Thomas on acoustic bass and Brian Blade on drums.

The album shows a different side of Redman. He let go of the traditional hard bop that characterised his earlier records and sought a connection with hip hop and urban dance rhythms. Leo Stanley of AllMusic found this engaging at times: where Redman played supple, appealing lines over the soft, sustained rhythms, the fusion worked. Too often, in his view, the record sounded forced and stiff. Even so, he felt that jazz and hip hop need a musician of Redman's calibre to be credible.
werk/joshua-redman-freedom-in-the-groove.listen: Listen to Hide and Seek and notice how the saxophone plays over a rhythm that is more reminiscent of hip hop than of hard bop.

werk/joshua-redman-timeless-tales-for-ch.text:
Timeless Tales (For Changing Times), from 1998, is saxophonist Joshua Redman's sixth album for Warner Bros. Many of the pieces are a tribute to the composers behind the title, from Gershwin and Kern to Stevie Wonder, Joni Mitchell, Bob Dylan, Cole Porter, Lennon and McCartney, and Prince. Between the songs are seven short Interludes that Redman wrote himself.

He plays tenor saxophone, with Brad Mehldau on piano, Larry Grenadier on bass and Brian Blade on drums. JazzTimes praised the band: Blade and Mehldau keep Redman out of sentimentality on I Had a King, and on one of the pieces Mehldau plays like a jazzy Glenn Gould. The Buffalo News called it a clever, pleasant standards record by a younger player who had done better before.
werk/joshua-redman-timeless-tales-for-ch.listen: Listen to The Times They Are a-Changin' and notice Brian Blade's cymbal and snare work and Brad Mehldau's piano.

werk/joshua-redman-wish.text:
Wish is saxophonist Joshua Redman's second studio album and was released in 1993 on Warner Bros. Records. He plays tenor saxophone, together with guitarist Pat Metheny, bassist Charlie Haden and drummer Billy Higgins. He said he wanted to work with them because they are masters and great storytellers. He was pleased with the result because of the clear shared identity and the organic unity.

Because Haden and Higgins played in Ornette Coleman's quartet, the record could have been avant-garde, but according to the AllMusic reviewer it is above all a post-bop album. He praised the jazz treatments of rock and rhythm and blues: Stevie Wonder's Make Sure You're Sure becomes a sombre jazz-noir mood, and Eric Clapton's Tears in Heaven changes from pop and rock into pop jazz. The album reached number 1 on the Billboard jazz albums chart.
werk/joshua-redman-wish.listen: Listen to Tears in Heaven, a song by Eric Clapton, and notice how the saxophone takes over the melody of a pop ballad and turns it into jazz.

werk/journey-infinity.text:
Infinity is Journey's fourth studio album, released in January 1978 by Columbia Records. It is the first album with singer Steve Perry and the last with drummer Aynsley Dunbar. Earlier the band had briefly worked with Robert Fleischman, but he was quickly replaced. Manager Herbie Herbert brought in producer Roy Thomas Baker, known for his work with Queen.

Baker built up a layered sound with stacked harmonies: each singer sang every part in unison, so that three or four voices sounded like many more. You hear that in Feeling That Way and Anytime. Patiently was the first song Perry and Schon wrote together, and Lights and Wheel in the Sky became singles. With Perry the group gained a more mainstream sound and had its biggest success so far.
werk/journey-infinity.listen: Listen to Anytime and notice the opening without instruments: the stacked voices already sound before the band comes in.

werk/journey-journey.text:
Journey is the band's debut album, released in April 1975 by Columbia Records. Unlike later records, it is mainly a progressive rock album in which the instrumental abilities of the musicians come first. It is the only album with rhythm guitarist George Tickner. The line-up otherwise consists of Gregg Rolie on keyboards and vocals, Neal Schon on lead guitar, Ross Valory on bass and Aynsley Dunbar on drums. Roy Halee produced.

Before the release the group had already recorded a demo album, with the same songs in a different order and with Prairie Prince on drums. There were more pieces, including instrumentals, that did not make the final record, such as Charge of the Light Brigade, the original title of that demo album.
werk/journey-journey.listen: Listen to Of a Lifetime and notice how much room the instruments are given: the record is mainly about the playing of the musicians.

werk/journey-look-into-the-future.text:
Look into the Future was released in January 1976 as the band's second album, again on Columbia Records. The members toned down the markedly progressive character of their debut and chose a more focused approach. Even so, some experimentation remained, especially in the title track and in I'm Gonna Leave You. The title track is the longest song the group ever recorded. There is also a cover of The Beatles' It's All Too Much, known from the film Yellow Submarine.

Rhythm guitarist George Tickner co-wrote two more songs, but then left the group. Four members remained: Gregg Rolie on keyboards and vocals, Neal Schon on guitar, Ross Valory on bass and Aynsley Dunbar on drums. Glen Kolotkin was co-producer and engineer.
werk/journey-look-into-the-future.listen: Listen to Look Into the Future, the longest track the band ever recorded, and notice how it remains experimental while the rest of the album is more focused.

werk/journey-next.text:
Next is the third studio album by the American rock band Journey, released in February 1977. The group continued the direction of Look into the Future, but also held on to something of the progressive rock of the first album. Gregg Rolie sings most of the songs; Neal Schon himself sings Karma and I Would Find You. Aynsley Dunbar plays drums.

Spaceman and Nickel and Dime were released together as a single. The album reached number 85 on the Billboard 200. In retrospect Martin Popoff praised the variety and the many good songs, from prog to sophisticated ballads. According to AllMusic the group still lacked a powerful singer. It was the last album on which Rolie was the main lead singer.
werk/journey-next.listen: Listen to Karma and notice the vocals of Neal Schon, who takes the lead himself here instead of Gregg Rolie.

werk/joy-division-closer.text:
Closer is Joy Division's second and last album. The band recorded it between 18 and 30 March 1980 at Britannia Row Studios in London, with producer Martin Hannett. Singer Ian Curtis took his own life two months later. The record was released on 18 July 1980 on Factory Records. The guitar songs had been written in late 1979, the songs with more synthesizers in early 1980.

The lyrics were strongly influenced by the fiction of J.G. Ballard. Atrocity Exhibition, the opening track, shares its title with a book by Ballard and features a Synare drum synthesizer run through a fuzz pedal. Hannett's production was praised as tomb-like, although Bernard Sumner and Peter Hook were not happy with it. The cover carries a photograph of a family tomb in Genoa. Closer received much praise at once and was named album of the year by NME. It is regarded as a milestone of post-punk.
werk/joy-division-closer.listen: Listen to Atrocity Exhibition and notice the rhythm: a Synare drum synthesizer, run through a fuzz pedal, sounds alongside the band.

werk/joy-division-unknown-pleasures.text:
Joy Division formed in 1976 in Salford, after Bernard Sumner and Peter Hook had seen a Sex Pistols gig. The debut was released in June 1979 on Factory Records. It was recorded and mixed over three weekends in April 1979 at Strawberry Studios in Stockport. Producer Martin Hannett used unusual techniques: digital delays, tape echo, the sound of breaking glass and a lift with a rotating loudspeaker. He recorded Ian Curtis's vocals in Insight over a telephone line to give them distance.

The band was divided over that spacious, dark sound. Sumner felt that Hannett had tamed the guitars, while Stephen Morris was pleased with it. Peter Saville designed the cover with a graph of the signals of a pulsar. No singles came from the album. It is regarded as an influential post-punk album and appears on many lists of the best albums of all time.
werk/joy-division-unknown-pleasures.listen: In Insight, listen to the vocals, which seem to come from far away. That is because the voice was recorded over a telephone line.

werk/juan-luis-guerra-4-40-bachata-rosa.text:
Bachata Rosa was released on 11 December 1990 on Karen Records and is the fifth album by Juan Luis Guerra and his group 4.40. Bachata was then considered the music of the Dominican countryside, with lyrics the public found too coarse, played on acoustic guitar with bongos and maracas. He began experimenting with the genre in collaboration with Sonia Silvestre, which produced Como Abeja al Panal. He wrote and produced everything himself and recorded at his own 4-40 studio in New York, with synthesizers.

The album has ten tracks, four of them bachata. Rosalía is a merengue and Como Abeja al Panal turns into salsa halfway through. La Bilirrubina is a merengue about a man in hospital with too much bilirubin from love and jealousy. Bachata Rosa was inspired by a poem by Pablo Neruda. The album brought bachata to a large audience and won a Grammy for Best Tropical Latin Album.
werk/juan-luis-guerra-4-40-bachata-rosa.listen: Listen to Como Abeja Al Panal and notice the moment halfway through when the bachata turns into salsa.

werk/judy-collins-a-maid-of-constant-sor.text:
On her 1961 debut album for Elektra, Judy Collins sings traditional folk songs. Her voice and guitar are sparingly accompanied by Fred Hellerman on second guitar and Erik Darling on banjo. Jac Holzman supervised the production.

The selection ranges from the Scottish Wild Mountain Thyme to Irish songs such as Bold Fenian Men and The Prickilie Bush. The title song is a variant of Man of Constant Sorrow. Many songs have the tone of a protest song, such as Ewan MacColl's Tim Evans, about a man who was wrongly hanged. In contrast there is the lively O Daddy Be Gay. The album sounds different from her later, better-known records and resembles Bob Dylan's first recordings.
werk/judy-collins-a-maid-of-constant-sor.listen: In Tim Evans, listen to the sparse accompaniment and to how the story of the wrongly convicted man is told.

werk/judy-collins-fifth-album.text:
Fifth Album was released in 1965 on Elektra Records. It is Judy Collins's fourth studio album, and her fifth release overall. Jac Holzman supervised the production. The record contains traditional ballads, alongside songs by singer-songwriters such as Bob Dylan, Richard Fariña, Phil Ochs and Malvina Reynolds.

A number of the songs are topical. Ochs's In the Heat of the Summer is about the Harlem riots of 1964, and Reynolds's It Isn't Nice is a protest song. The last track is a live recording from Town Hall in New York in March 1964. Collins sings and plays guitar and keyboards, with, among others, Richard Fariña on dulcimer, John Sebastian on harmonica and Eric Weissberg as second guitarist. In this way she stands between traditional folk and the new songs of Dylan. The album reached number 69 on the Billboard chart.
werk/judy-collins-fifth-album.listen: Listen to Mr. Tambourine Man and notice how Collins sings Dylan's song in her own way.

werk/judy-collins-golden-apples-of-the-s.text:
Judy Collins's second studio album was released in 1962 on Elektra. Jac Holzman supervised the production. Collins plays guitar and keyboards, Walter Raim plays second guitar and Bill Lee bass.

The title song sets William Butler Yeats's poem The Song of Wandering Aengus to music by Collins herself. The rest consists mainly of traditional songs, from Great Selchie of Shule Skerry to Shule Aroon, supplemented with songs by Sydney Carter and Mike Settle. Bruce Eder of AllMusic hears a more attractive sound and a freer approach than on her debut, and The Washington Post called the title song brilliant. The record shows her still in her traditional folk period.
werk/judy-collins-golden-apples-of-the-s.listen: In Golden Apples of the Sun, listen to how the music carries the words of Yeats.

werk/judy-collins-in-my-life.text:
In My Life is Judy Collins's fifth studio album and was released in 1966 on Elektra Records. Her earlier records had consisted mainly of straightforward folk. Now she worked with arranger Joshua Rifkin, who wrote orchestral arrangements for many of the songs. That was a clear step away from her previous work.

The record contains songs by Leonard Cohen, the Beatles, Bob Dylan and Richard Fariña. Collins's version of Suzanne is regarded as the recording that introduced Cohen's music to a large audience. The album reached number forty-six on the Billboard chart in 1967 and was certified gold in 1970. Reviewer William Ruhlmann later called it largely an excellent album and one of her best. He saw in the record a singer broadening her horizons.
werk/judy-collins-in-my-life.listen: Listen to Suzanne and notice how a song by Leonard Cohen takes on its own colour in Collins's voice.

werk/junkie-xl-big-sounds-of-the-drags.text:
Big Sounds of the Drags is the second album by the Dutch electronic musician Junkie XL. It was released in 1999 on Roadrunner Records. The cover shows the Funny Car named Black Magic, a 1977 Chevy Vega belonging to RC Sherman. A reissue with a different track selection followed in 2000.

The album is a mixture of electronic music with guitars by, among others, Dino Cazares and Max Cavalera. Tom Holkenborg, the man behind the project, produced and programmed most of it himself, with vocals by Patrick Tilon. The music found its way into other media: Synasthesia, Dance USA and Future in Computer Hell (Part II) appeared in the racing game Test Drive: Overdrive, Action Radius in Need for Speed: Underground, and Zerotonine was heard in the film Buying the Cow.
werk/junkie-xl-big-sounds-of-the-drags.listen: Listen to Action Radius, a track with vocals by Patrick Tilon, and notice how voice and electronic beats come together.

werk/junkie-xl-saturday-teenage-kick.text:
Saturday Teenage Kick, from 1997, is the first studio album by the Dutch electronic musician Junkie XL, behind whom Tom Holkenborg is hiding. He produced, wrote, mixed and programmed the record himself and also played keyboards, bass and guitar. Guest guitarists are Rene van der Zee and Dino Cazares, and Baz Mattie plays drums.

Patrick Tilon sings on the album; he is also the rapper Rude Boy of Urban Dance Squad. The record has twelve tracks. The last, Future in Computer Hell, lasts almost eighteen minutes and in some editions hides an extra track, Mulu. Notable is an unusual aftermath: in 1998 several tracks appeared under other names on The Castbreeder, a fake album by The Prodigy.
werk/junkie-xl-saturday-teenage-kick.listen: Listen to Saturday Teenage Kick and notice how electronic programming and played instruments come together.

werk/junkie-xl-today.text:
Today is the fourth album by the Dutch producer Tom Holkenborg, who works under the name Junkie XL. It was released in 2006. Nathan Mader sings on a number of tracks, and Holkenborg himself plays acoustic and electric guitar.

Honey is dedicated to the mother of his then fiancée and named after her. His ex-fiancée Carolyn sings on I've Got a Xerox to Copy. The title track Today got a second life in the computer games Burnout Legends and Burnout Revenge and, in 2008, in ESPN commercials for Major League Soccer. A snippet of the melody of Even In This Moment sounds the same when you play it backwards.
werk/junkie-xl-today.listen: Listen to Today, the track that was heard in the Burnout games, and notice what the electric guitar adds to the electronic foundation.

werk/justin-bieber-under-the-mistletoe.text:
Under the Mistletoe is Justin Bieber's first Christmas album and his second studio album. It was released on 1 November 2011. On 25 August he announced the project, and the guests were revealed later: Usher, Boyz II Men, The Band Perry, Busta Rhymes and Mariah Carey, with whom he recorded All I Want for Christmas Is You as a duet. The album contains seven original songs, co-written by him, alongside covers of Christmas carols and standards. Mistletoe, made with producers The Messengers, was the first single. Santa Claus Is Coming to Town uses samples of I Want You Back and ABC by the Jackson 5.

The reviews were mixed. Many critics found the original songs better than the classics, and some felt that the guests stole the show. The album did debut at number one on the American Billboard 200.
werk/justin-bieber-under-the-mistletoe.listen: In Santa Claus Is Coming to Town, listen for whether you recognise the Jackson 5 samples.

werk/kamasi-washington-heaven-and-earth.text:
Heaven and Earth is saxophonist Kamasi Washington's fourth album and the follow-up to his triple album The Epic. It was released on 22 June 2018 and lasts almost two and a half hours. It consists of two CDs: Earth deals with earthly matters, Heaven with utopian thinking. There is also a hidden extra disc, The Choice, in a sealed section of the packaging. The sound does not differ much between the two discs. It is jazz with a large orchestra and choir, played by a band of Los Angeles musicians who have been playing together for years.

Critics called it more focused than The Epic, with less wandering and many colourful contrasts. The Guardian made it album of the week and Pitchfork gave it Best New Music. Some felt that his playing as a soloist remains limited, but his strength as a composer and arranger is widely praised.
werk/kamasi-washington-heaven-and-earth.listen: In Fists of Fury, listen to Washington's saxophone. Notice his muscular, centred tone and how steady the rhythm beneath it is.

werk/kamasi-washington-the-epic.text:
Kamasi Washington grew up in Los Angeles and from a young age built up his collective, the West Coast Get Down. His old acquaintance Flying Lotus, known for the label Brainfeeder, offered him the chance to record an album and gave him complete creative freedom. In December 2011 the collective rented Kingsize Soundlabs in Los Angeles for a month. The sessions were busy: there were two bassists, two drummers and two keyboard players, and singer Patrice Quinn sang from the control room. From about 190 recorded tracks, Washington chose seventeen.

He added an orchestra of 32 players and a choir of twenty singers, for which he wrote the arrangements himself. This made it a triple album, built around a story he remembered from a recurring dream. The critical response was glowing. AllMusic called it twenty-first-century jazz that is accessible and virtuosic at the same time, and Pitchfork gave it the tag Best New Music.
werk/kamasi-washington-the-epic.listen: Listen to Change of the Guard and notice how the orchestra and the choir, together with the band, form a very big sound.

werk/kanda-bongo-man-zing-zong.text:
Zing-Zong, from 1991, is an album by the Congolese singer Kanda Bongo Man, dedicated to two brothers from the soukous band Orchestre Bella Bella, Soki Vangu and Soki Dianzenza. They died within a year of each other. Freres Soki is a tribute to them, and the title track is an adaptation of their hit Houleux Houleux. The singer produced the record himself, sang in Lingala and French and took the album on a tour of North America. Nene Tchakou plays the guitar.

The press was positive but not unanimous. The Washington Post heard a fluid weave of sparkling guitars, light rolling rhythms and soft soul vocals. The Boston Herald noted the added horns on top of the Zairean rumba. Another newspaper found the endlessly repeated beat tiring in the end.
werk/kanda-bongo-man-zing-zong.listen: Listen to Zing-Zong, the adaptation of a hit by Orchestre Bella Bella, and notice how the guitars interweave above the light, rolling rhythms.

werk/kanye-west-808s-en-heartbreak.text:
808s & Heartbreak is Kanye West's fourth studio album, released on 24 November 2008. He recorded it in about three weeks, in September and October 2008, in Burbank, California and in Honolulu, Hawaii. The occasion was the death of his mother Donda in November 2007 and the end of his engagement to Alexis Phifer in April 2008. He was also struggling with his new pop-star status.

He broke with his earlier hip hop: he mostly sings instead of rapping, with Auto-Tune over a bare, electronic accompaniment with a lot of minor keys and the Roland TR-808 drum machine. The title refers to it. The album was about loss and heartbreak. The public was at first taken aback, but the reviews were positive. Critics see it as one of his most influential records for hip hop, pop and R&B.
werk/kanye-west-808s-en-heartbreak.listen: Listen to Heartless and notice the vocals with Auto-Tune and the tight, almost bare drum machine beneath.

werk/kanye-west-graduation.text:
Graduation is Kanye West's third studio album, released on 11 September 2007 on Def Jam and Roc-A-Fella. He recorded it between 2005 and 2007 in New York and Los Angeles and produced most of it himself. After a tour with U2, he wanted to make big songs for stadiums. He drew inspiration from house and indie rock, used layered synthesizers and rapped more smoothly. In doing so he left the soulful sound of his earlier records behind. He left out skits, because in his view they weakened the listening experience.

The lyrics sketch a mixed feeling about his fame, with messages of triumph. Stronger was an international hit and reached number 1 on the American Hot 100. The album received praise for its production and won a Grammy for Best Rap Album. It was released on the same day as 50 Cent's Curtis.
werk/kanye-west-graduation.listen: Listen to Stronger and notice how electronic sounds and a big, sing-along chorus take the place of soul samples.

werk/kanye-west-late-registration.text:
After the success of The College Dropout, Kanye West did not want to make the same record again. His sped-up soul samples were widely imitated by other rappers. For his second album he spent a year working in Hollywood and New York with Jon Brion. Together they built a richer, orchestral sound, with an ensemble of twenty musicians and instruments rarely heard in hip hop, such as a celesta, a harpsichord and Chinese bells. West drew inspiration from Fiona Apple and Portishead. He originally wrote Gold Digger for another rapper, after which Jamie Foxx added the vocals from a Ray Charles song.

The record received glowing reviews and was seen as a step forward. It entered the American chart at number one and earned West eight Grammy nominations.
werk/kanye-west-late-registration.listen: Listen to Gold Digger and notice Jamie Foxx's vocals, which refer to a Ray Charles song, and the extra instruments Jon Brion added to the track.

werk/kanye-west-the-college-dropout.text:
Kanye West had been making beats for others for years, including Jay-Z and Talib Kweli, but the music world did not take him seriously as an artist. He signed with Roc-A-Fella and from 1999 worked for four years on his debut. In 2002 he broke his jaw in a car accident, and two weeks later he recorded a track with his jaw still wired shut. The record was produced mainly by West himself and has a sound known as chipmunk soul: sped-up voices from old soul and R&B, his own drum programming, strings and gospel choirs.

Instead of the gangster persona that was usual in hip hop at the time, West rapped about family, doubt, materialism, faith, racism and going to college. The record received glowing reviews and won a Grammy for Best Rap Album. Many magazines count it among the best albums ever.
werk/kanye-west-the-college-dropout.listen: Listen to Jesus Walks and notice the military-sounding beats and the choir, while West raps about faith and about the way the media avoid the subject.

werk/kate-bush-50-words-for-snow.text:
Kate Bush released this album on 21 November 2011 on her own label Fish People. It was her second record of that year, after Director's Cut, and her first entirely new material since Aerial in 2005. The seven songs are set against a background of falling snow and together last 65 minutes. Lake Tahoe and Misty are the longest songs in her work.

The music revolves around calm, jazzy piano playing and Steve Gadd's drums, with both sung and spoken voice. Snowflake opens with the high choirboy voice of her son Albert. In Wild Man, mountaineers out of compassion hide the Yeti's footprints. Elton John sings along on Snowed In at Wheeler Street, and Stephen Fry recites the title song with invented snow words. Among Angels closes as a subdued love song. The album received wide praise.
werk/kate-bush-50-words-for-snow.listen: Listen to Snowflake and notice the high choirboy voice of Albert, who sings the role of the falling snowflake.

werk/kate-bush-hounds-of-love.text:
In the summer of 1983 Kate Bush began work on this album at home, with a LinnDrum, a Fairlight and a piano. Her previous record, The Dreaming, had sold poorly. After recording sessions in London and Ireland, and a year of overdubbing and mixing, Hounds of Love was finished in June 1985. The album came out on 16 September and consists of two parts. The first side contains the singles Running Up That Hill, Hounds of Love, The Big Sky and Cloudbusting. The second side is called The Ninth Wave and tells, as a suite, of a woman drifting alone in the sea at night.

In the title track, lines from the horror film Night of the Demon are sampled. Running Up That Hill became her biggest hit. The album reached first place in England and received much praise. It is often counted among the best albums of all time and is her best-selling studio album.
werk/kate-bush-hounds-of-love.listen: Listen to Hounds of Love and notice at the beginning the spoken line from an old horror film, which is sampled here.

werk/kate-bush-lionheart.text:
Nine months after her successful debut, the record company EMI wanted a second album quickly. She was only nineteen and had already written many songs as a teenager. Of the ten tracks, only three were new: Symphony in Blue, Fullhouse and Coffee Homeground. The rest dated from before her debut and were reworked. The album was recorded at Super Bear Studios on the French Riviera, the only time she recorded outside England. Andrew Powell was producer again, because she still felt too inexperienced to do it herself. Del Palmer played on it for the first time.

The lyrics refer to Peter Pan, Hammer films and police series. Hammer Horror did not make the top 40, while Wow reached number 14. The press was lukewarm and she found the album too rushed, although she was pleased with Wow. The album stayed 36 weeks in the British charts and went platinum.
werk/kate-bush-lionheart.listen: Listen to Wow and notice the lyrics about the music world and show business, and how she sings about it.

werk/kate-bush-never-for-ever.text:
After her 1979 tour Kate Bush began her third album, and for the first time she took charge of the production herself, together with Jon Kelly. She let go of arranger Andrew Powell, who had orchestrated the first two albums, because she wanted to make more choices of her own. As a result the album sounds more varied, from the rocker Violin to the wistful waltz Army Dreamers. Digital synthesizers and drum machines, such as the Fairlight CMI, were used for the first time.

The songs draw heavily on film and literature. The Infant Kiss is based on the film The Innocents and Delius (Song of Summer) on a television film by Ken Russell about the composer Delius. Blow Away is a tribute to her lighting director Bill Duffield, who was killed in an accident during a tour. The album was released in 1980 and reached number 1 in England, a first for a British female solo artist. Babooshka became one of her biggest hits. Critics were mostly positive.
werk/kate-bush-never-for-ever.listen: Listen to Babooshka and notice how the story unfolds in the song and how the vocals carry the story.

werk/kate-bush-the-dreaming.text:
For her fourth album the singer decided to produce herself, after working with Jon Kelly on the previous one. She worked on the record for two years, mainly with the Fairlight, a sampler, and with several engineers, including Nick Launay. The first demo, for Sat in Your Lap, was made in September 1980 after a Stevie Wonder concert. The album was released on 13 September 1982 and sounds experimental, with mandolins, uilleann pipes and didgeridoos, changing time signatures and samples. The songs are about, among other things, old crime films, the war in Vietnam, the Aboriginals and Houdini.

The record entered the English chart at number three, but sold less than the earlier ones. The press called it uncommercial, and reactions were divided. In the decades that followed, appreciation rose sharply, and musicians such as Björk name the album as a favourite.
werk/kate-bush-the-dreaming.listen: Listen to Sat in Your Lap, the first track to be released. Notice how full and busy the production sounds.

werk/kate-bush-the-kick-inside.text:
Kate Bush had been writing songs since she was eleven and recorded demos with the help of her brothers. Through a friend, these reached David Gilmour of Pink Floyd in 1972. He was impressed, paid for better demos and played them to record executives. EMI signed her, with already about a hundred songs to her name. In July and August 1977 the rest of the record was recorded at AIR Studios in London, under producer Andrew Powell, with experienced session musicians.

Wuthering Heights was inspired by a 1967 television series, not by the novel itself. Bush insisted that this song be the first single, and it spent four weeks at the top of the British chart. The album reached third place in the United Kingdom and received praise both immediately and later.
werk/kate-bush-the-kick-inside.listen: Listen to Wuthering Heights and notice Bush's voice, which sounds remarkably high and expressive for a pop single.

werk/kate-bush-the-red-shoes.text:
The Red Shoes was released on 1 November 1993 and was Kate Bush's last record before a break of twelve years. The title comes from the 1948 film by Michael Powell and Emeric Pressburger, which is based on the fairy tale by Hans Christian Andersen: a dancer can no longer take off her shoes. While making it she lost her mother and her guitarist Alan Murphy, and her long relationship with bassist Del Palmer ended.

She aimed for a live band sound, with fewer studio tricks than on earlier records. There are remarkably many guests. Prince plays and sings on Why Should I Love You?, Eric Clapton plays guitar on And So Is Love and Trio Bulgarka sings on three tracks. She also made the short film The Line, the Cross and the Curve. The album reached number two in the British chart.
werk/kate-bush-the-red-shoes.listen: Listen to And So Is Love and notice Eric Clapton's guitar alongside the vocals.

werk/kate-bush-the-sensual-world.text:
The Sensual World is Kate Bush's sixth album and was released in October 1989 on EMI. For the title song she drew inspiration from James Joyce's Ulysses. Her music suited Molly Bloom's closing monologue, but the Joyce estate would not release the text. Bush therefore wrote her own words, in which Molly steps out of the book and discovers the real world. Beneath her singing sound Irish instruments such as uilleann pipes, fiddle and flute. On three tracks the Bulgarian vocal ensemble Trio Bulgarka sings along, and David Gilmour plays guitar.

The album reached number 2 in England. A Q reviewer heard an erratic collection of moods held together by her voice, with a dreamy atmosphere and solid chords in Love and Anger. In 2011 she re-recorded the title song as Flower of the Mountain, with Joyce's original text, after the estate had given permission after all.
werk/kate-bush-the-sensual-world.listen: In The Sensual World, listen to the Irish pipes that sway beneath the vocals, and notice how the song slowly builds.

werk/kayak-royal-bed-bouncer.text:
Royal Bed Bouncer was, in 1975, the third album by the Dutch progressive rock group Kayak. Nine of the ten songs were written by keyboardist Ton Scherpenzeel. Only the instrumental Patricia Anglaia came from drummer Pim Koopman. Gerrit-Jan Leenders and the band themselves produced the record. In the Netherlands it was released on EMI, in the United States on Janus Records, with a different cover.

Chance For A Lifetime was the only single and reached twentieth place in the Dutch chart. In 1997 this line-up reunited for a Dutch television programme in the series Classic Albums. Together with a few concerts, that eventually led in 1999 to a restart of the group.
werk/kayak-royal-bed-bouncer.listen: In Chance For A Lifetime, listen to the keyboards and to how Max Werner's vocals carry the chorus.

werk/kayak-see-see-the-sun.text:
See See the Sun is the first album by Kayak, a Dutch progressive rock band. It came out in 1973 on Harvest Records. The line-up consisted of Max Werner on vocals, Johan Slager on guitar, Ton Scherpenzeel on keyboards, Cees van Leeuwen on bass guitar and Pim Koopman on drums. Koopman also sang the lead part himself in Lovely Luna and Forever Is a Lonely Thought.

The best-known and strangest track is Mammoth. It is one of the few pop singles with a barrel organ. The organ, De Flamingo, was too big to get into the studio, so the melody was recorded outside. Because the organ is operated by hand, the tempo kept changing, and that made it very hard to fit the piece into the rest of the song. On Lyrics, guests played violin and cello.
werk/kayak-see-see-the-sun.listen: Listen to Mammoth and notice the barrel organ: hear how the organ's tempo wavers slightly against the rest of the band.

werk/kayak-the-last-encore.text:
The Last Encore is the fourth album by the Dutch progressive rock group Kayak. It came out in 1976 on Vertigo Records. The line-up consisted of singer Max Werner, guitarist Johan Slager, keyboardist Ton Scherpenzeel, bassist Bert Veldkamp and drummer Pim Koopman. Werner sings almost all the songs; Koopman sings the last one himself, Well Done.

Besides the usual instruments, you hear Mellotron, accordion, marimba and zither, among others. In the Netherlands Still My Heart Cries For You and Do You Care were released as singles, but neither reached the top 40. After this album Koopman left to become a record producer. In 1999 he returned. In the United States the record was not released. There, Janus Records released an album titled Starlight Dancer, with songs from two European records.
werk/kayak-the-last-encore.listen: In Still My Heart Cries for You, listen to Max Werner's vocals and notice the role of the keyboard work in the song.

werk/keith-jarrett-life-between-the-exit.text:
Life Between the Exit Signs is Keith Jarrett's first jazz album as a leader. It was recorded on 4 May 1967 at Atlantic Recording Studios in New York and released in April 1968 on Vortex, a subsidiary label of Atlantic. It was the first time Jarrett, bassist Charlie Haden and drummer Paul Motian played together. Producer George Avakian made sure he could choose his own musicians and left the music completely untouched.

The three played differently: Haden had played with Ornette Coleman, Motian with Bill Evans, and both influences can be heard. The programme consists of original pieces and a Cole Porter standard, with Lisbon Stomp as the opener. Critics heard a pianist who already had a recognisable voice, although the group was not yet the unit that would follow later.
werk/keith-jarrett-life-between-the-exit.listen: In Lisbon Stomp, listen to the opening melody and the fast runs with which the pianist begins his solo.

werk/keith-jarrett-restoration-ruin.text:
Restoration Ruin is an oddity in Keith Jarrett's catalogue. Here he plays almost all the instruments himself, including piano, organ, guitar, soprano saxophone, harmonica and drums, and sings his own lyrics. The record was released in 1968 on Vortex, a subsidiary label of Atlantic. The sound is mainly influenced by folk and progressive rock, and the album is regarded as the beginning of an experimental period, outside jazz and classical.

Sioux City Sue New was also released as a single. Critical opinion is divided. Richie Unterberger of AllMusic gave two and a half stars and heard alternating Dylan-like songs and baroque-folk pieces. Ian Carr called the singing and lyrics weak, and producer George Avakian said the idea came from Jarrett. The Penguin Guide found it a convincing exercise in instrumental versatility.
werk/keith-jarrett-restoration-ruin.listen: In Sioux City Sue New, listen to the vocals and the accompaniment, and bear in mind that one and the same musician plays almost everything.

werk/keith-jarrett-the-mourning-of-a-sta.text:
Keith Jarrett recorded this album in 1971 with his regular trio: bassist Charlie Haden and drummer Paul Motian. In July and August of that year, over five days, he made enough music for three albums, together with saxophonist Dewey Redman. Redman does not play on this record, but the sessions formed the transition from Jarrett's first trio to the later quartet. Atlantic Records released the album that same year.

The music partly follows the traditional avant-garde piano trio of earlier records, but the sound is richer and more colourful. Jarrett also plays soprano saxophone, flute and other instruments. Traces of You features him as a soprano saxophonist. Standing Outside is by himself and All I Want is by Joni Mitchell. In JazzTimes, Kenny Werner wrote that the album is an early sign of the combination of melodic music and adventurous free improvisation.
werk/keith-jarrett-the-mourning-of-a-sta.listen: Listen to Traces of You and notice the soprano saxophone: here Jarrett is not only a pianist, but also a soloist on another instrument.

werk/keith-sweat-get-up-on-it.text:
Get Up on It is the fourth studio album by the American R&B singer Keith Sweat. Elektra Records released it on 28 June 1994. It spent two weeks at the top of Billboard's R&B and hip hop albums chart and reached number eight on the Billboard 200. A platinum certification followed on 6 December 1994.

The singles were How Do You Like It?, When I Give My Love and the title song. He co-wrote and co-produced, together with, among others, Jerry Flowers and Eric McCaine. There are guests: Left Eye of TLC, Roger Troutman of Zapp and the up-and-coming group Kut Klose, with Athena Cage. The album has fourteen tracks, including an interlude and an intermission.
werk/keith-sweat-get-up-on-it.listen: Listen to When I Give My Love and notice how the vocals carry the song.

werk/keith-sweat-i-ll-give-all-my-love-t.text:
I'll Give All My Love to You is Keith Sweat's second studio album and came out on 12 June 1990. It was his last record on Vincent Davis's Vintertainment label, which shortly afterwards severed its ties with Elektra. Sweat produced the album himself, together with, among others, Teddy Riley and Bobby Wooten.

According to Rolling Stone, the album is about love that is lost, found and won back, and about lust, over heavy synthesizer rhythms. Make You Sweat and the title song became his second and third number 1 hits on the R&B chart, and both also reached the pop top 20. Merry Go Round and Your Love Part 2 reached the top 5 of the R&B chart. The album reached number 1 on the R&B albums chart and number 6 on the Billboard 200. A Los Angeles Times reviewer missed Riley's input as a producer.
werk/keith-sweat-i-ll-give-all-my-love-t.listen: Listen to Make You Sweat and notice the tight synthesizer groove on which Sweat's vocals sit.

werk/keith-sweat-keep-it-comin.text:
Keep It Comin' is the third studio album by the American R&B singer Keith Sweat and was released on 26 November 1991. It entered at number one on the R&B albums chart straight away and was also in the top twenty of the Billboard 200. For three weeks it kept Michael Jackson's Dangerous from first place. On 21 February 1992 it was certified platinum.

The title song was his fourth single to top the R&B chart. I Want to Love You Down and Why Me Baby reached the top twenty of the same chart. There is also a song that had appeared a few months earlier on the soundtrack of the film New Jack City, There You Go (Tellin' Me No Again). It was the last album on which he worked with the new jack swing producer Teddy Riley, until Just Me sixteen years later.
werk/keith-sweat-keep-it-comin.listen: Listen to Keep It Comin', the title song and his fourth number one on the R&B chart. Notice how the vocals carry the song.

werk/keith-sweat-make-it-last-forever.text:
Make It Last Forever is the debut album by the American R&B singer Keith Sweat and was released on 24 November 1987. He made it together with Teddy Riley, whom he knew from the New York band competitions. They recorded it at INS Recording and Power Play Studios in New York. The work took six months. Sixteen or seventeen songs were recorded, but only eight made the record. Riley convinced Sweat to sing I Want Her in a nasal voice.

The album is regarded as one of the first R&B records with the sound of new jack swing. It spent three weeks at the top of the R&B albums chart. I Want Her became the first number 1 hit on that chart, followed by the title song, a duet with Jacci McGhee. Critics praised his pleading tenor, and Allmusic sees it as his best album.
werk/keith-sweat-make-it-last-forever.listen: Listen to I Want Her and notice the nasal singing voice and the drum machine beneath: this is how new jack swing sounded in 1987.

werk/kelly-clarkson-all-i-ever-wanted.text:
After the quarrels surrounding the dark My December, Kelly Clarkson opted for a lighter, more pop-oriented album, which was released on 6 March 2009 on RCA Records. She worked with old acquaintances such as Max Martin, Dr. Luke, Sam Watters and Louis Biancaniello, and with new collaborators such as Ryan Tedder, Howard Benson and Dre & Vidal. The working title was Masquerade, until it seemed too similar to the titles of other albums of the time.

The songs are about relationships, dignity, independence and honesty, with pop punk, dance and soul alongside pop. My Life Would Suck Without You, the first single, became her second number one on the American Hot 100. Already Gone led to discussion, because it resembled Beyoncé's Halo. Critics praised her singing and her approach to the mainstream, although a few called the album over-produced. The album received a Grammy nomination for Best Pop Vocal Album.
werk/kelly-clarkson-all-i-ever-wanted.listen: Listen to Already Gone and compare it with Beyoncé's Halo: can you hear why critics noticed the similarity?

werk/kelly-clarkson-breakaway.text:
Breakaway is Kelly Clarkson's second album and was released on 30 November 2004 on RCA Records. After her debut Thankful, critics continued to see her mainly as the winner of American Idol. She therefore sought out new writers and producers, including Dr. Luke, Max Martin, John Shanks, Kara DioGuardi and the former Evanescence members Ben Moody and David Hodges. She co-wrote about half of the album herself. It became a pop record with rock and soul, unlike the more R&B-oriented debut.

Since U Been Gone, Behind These Hazel Eyes, Because of You, Walk Away and Breakaway became hits worldwide. Breakaway was originally written for Avril Lavigne's debut and appeared on the soundtrack of The Princess Diaries 2. The album won the Grammy for Best Pop Vocal Album. In the United States it reached number three and was certified six times platinum. According to Billboard, the singer helped shape the uptempo, dance-oriented pop sound of the 2000s.
werk/kelly-clarkson-breakaway.listen: Listen to Since U Been Gone and notice how pop and rock come together here.

werk/kelly-clarkson-my-december.text:
After the success of Breakaway in 2004, Kelly Clarkson began on new songs during her tour. She wrote about sixty songs, a process she called free therapy, after a gruelling tour and a broken relationship. With producer David Kahne she made My December, which came out on 22 June 2007 on RCA Records. The album took on a darker, more personal tone, with Alanis Morissette's Jagged Little Pill as inspiration.

Clive Davis, the head of Sony BMG, reportedly wanted major changes, because he missed a sure radio hit. Clarkson refused to alter the songs. The record sounds like alternative rock, hard rock and pop rock, with influences of blues, country and soul. Never Again became the best-known single and reached number eight on the American Hot 100. Irvine is about the day she cancelled a meeting with fans through exhaustion. Critics praised her courage and her songs, although some found the execution uneven.
werk/kelly-clarkson-my-december.listen: Listen to Never Again, the first single, and notice how the song combines pop and rock.

werk/kelly-clarkson-thankful.text:
Thankful is Kelly Clarkson's debut and came out on 15 April 2003 on RCA Records. In September 2002 she had won the first season of American Idol. She then recorded with many different writers and producers, including Babyface, Desmond Child, Cathy Dennis and The Underdogs. The release was pushed back from November 2002, because of her busy schedule and the search for suitable material. She co-wrote four of the twelve songs and had to fight for uptempo songs, because the label preferred ballads. There are four covers, including Some Kind of Miracle, Anytime and Just Missed the Train.

Miss Independent became her first international hit and earned a first Grammy nomination. The Trouble with Love Is appeared on the soundtrack of Love Actually. The album entered at number one in the United States. Critics praised her voice and versatility, but found the record too heavily produced and too closely tied to the talent show.
werk/kelly-clarkson-thankful.listen: Listen to Miss Independent, the single with which she broke through internationally, and notice how her voice carries the song.

werk/kendrick-lamar-damn.text:
DAMN. was released on 14 April 2017 as Kendrick Lamar's fourth album. He brought in many producers, including Sounwave, DJ Dahi and Mike Will Made It, and had guests such as Rihanna, Zacari and U2. The album is counted among conscious hip hop, with trap, R&B and pop running through it. Mike Will originally made the beat of Humble for a recording with Gucci Mane, until Lamar kept it for himself. On DNA he rapped the second verse a cappella and had the beat built around it, so that it sounds like a fight with the beat.

Humble became his first number 1 on the American Hot 100. The album topped the Billboard 200 and won the Grammy for Best Rap Album. In 2018 it earned him the Pulitzer Prize for Music, the first time for an artist from outside classical music and jazz. A Collectors Edition with a reversed track list was released later.
werk/kendrick-lamar-damn.listen: Listen to DNA and notice the second part of the song, where the beat changes and the rap sounds like a fight with the music.

werk/kendrick-lamar-gnx.text:
Kendrick Lamar began this album just after 2022's Mr. Morale & the Big Steppers, with producers Sounwave and Jack Antonoff. They recorded eighty to a hundred songs, of which twelve made the record. The title refers to the Buick Grand National Experimental, a car he had bought. GNX was released as a surprise on 22 November 2024, his first album after leaving Top Dawg Entertainment and Aftermath.

At just over 44 minutes it is his shortest studio album. The record is a tribute to his home city of Los Angeles, with plenty of G-funk. The Mexican singer Deyra Barrera sings on three tracks. Reincarnated uses the music of Tupac Shakur's Made Niggaz. Squabble Up and Luther reached the top of the Hot 100. Critics saw a successful new take on West Coast hip hop. The album won four Grammys, including Best Rap Album.
werk/kendrick-lamar-gnx.listen: In luther, listen to the sample of Marvin Gaye's If This World Were Mine, sung by Luther Vandross. Notice how soft it sounds on an album full of hard hip hop.

werk/kendrick-lamar-good-kid-m-a-a-d-cit.text:
After the independently released Section.80 from 2011, Kendrick Lamar signed with Interscope and Dr. Dre's Aftermath. His second album, released on 22 October 2012, was his first for a major label. It was recorded mainly in studios in California, with Dr. Dre, Just Blaze, Pharrell Williams and Hit-Boy, among others, as producers. The cover carries the description short film by Kendrick Lamar.

The album tells, in a non-linear story, of his youth in Compton, amid drugs and gang violence. The production is subdued and atmospheric, with subtle hooks, tight bass and light piano. The first song he recorded was Compton with Dr. Dre. Critics praised the thematic scope and the lyrics. The album received seven Grammy nominations, including Album of the Year, and in 2022 Rolling Stone named it the best concept album of all time.
werk/kendrick-lamar-good-kid-m-a-a-d-cit.listen: Listen to Compton, the first song recorded for this album, and notice how love for the city and concern about its condition run together.

werk/kendrick-lamar-to-pimp-a-butterfly.text:
Kendrick Lamar's third album came out on 15 March 2015. While making it he travelled to South Africa, where he visited, among other things, Nelson Mandela's cell on Robben Island. That trip determined the direction of the album, and he threw away material for two or three albums. Dr. Dre was executive producer, alongside Sounwave, Terrace Martin, Thundercat and Flying Lotus, among others.

At its core it is a hip hop album, but it draws on the whole history of African-American music, especially jazz, funk and soul. The lyrics deal with racism, inequality, depression and Black culture. Wesley's Theory opens the album with George Clinton and Thundercat, and Complexion (A Zulu Love) with Rapsody is about light and dark skin colour. Critics praised the musical breadth and the social charge. The album won a Grammy for Best Rap Album and in 2020 stood at number 19 on Rolling Stone's list.
werk/kendrick-lamar-to-pimp-a-butterfly.listen: Listen to Wesley's Theory and notice the funky foundation and the moment when George Clinton's voice comes in.

werk/kenny-clarke-pieces-of-time.text:
Pieces of Time is an album by four jazz drummers: Kenny Clarke, Andrew Cyrille, Milford Graves and Famoudou Don Moye. Cyrille set the project in motion. They recorded it in September 1983 in New York; it was released in 1984 on the Soul Note label. Each drummer contributed compositions, and in addition each played a personal two-minute statement.

Max Roach wrote the liner notes and called the idea of four percussionists taking sound as their starting point a purely artistic design. The Penguin Guide to Jazz wrote that Clarke, the eldest of the group, almost stole the show. Robert Palmer remarked in The New York Times that Clarke had never stopped listening to younger players. The reviews also praised the coherence of the group pieces.
werk/kenny-clarke-pieces-of-time.listen: Listen to Pieces of Time (Personal Statements) and notice the four different drummers: how does the sound and approach of each of them differ?

werk/kenny-clarke-telefunken-blues.text:
Telefunken Blues actually consists of two sessions. The first was recorded on 1 November 1954 in Hollywood, with Milt Jackson and Percy Heath of the Modern Jazz Quartet, saxophonists Frank Morgan and Walter Benton and pianist Gerald Wiggins. The second followed on 7 February 1955 at Van Gelder Studio in Hackensack, New Jersey, with members of Count Basie's band and arranger Ernie Wilkins. Drummer Kenny Clarke leads both groups. The album was released on the Savoy label.

On the first four tracks, such as Strollin' and Sonor, Jackson plays vibraphone. On the last four, including Telefunken Blues and Klook's Nook, he sits at the piano and a larger ensemble with trombone, flute and baritone saxophone can be heard. Jim Todd's review on Allmusic found everyone in good form, but the 1954 session the most interesting.
werk/kenny-clarke-telefunken-blues.listen: Listen to Telefunken Blues and notice Milt Jackson's piano, whom you also hear on vibraphone on this album. Can you hear how the horns play around him?
